newsitem.title: UK: LME copper gives back gains in late trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper gives back gains in late trade.

text.p: London metal Exchange (LME) copper prices gave back most of the day's gains in the evening session after attempted rallies earlier failed, traders said.
By 1800 GMT the three months red metal contract was indicated at $1,935/$1,938 about $9 down from the kerb close and and barely a couple of dollars above Monday's kerb level.
As prices approached the key $1,970 per tonne level on the first afternoon ring, selling came in to stall the advance at $1,968 on profit-taking and producer selling.
It disappointed further by failing to stay above the $1,950 level, traders said.
Aluminium also edged lower after coming off highs and closing the kerb at a $30 firmer $1,356.
Later business was quiet but indications were around $1,348/$1,350.

There was little movement among the other metals but lead was down about $3 fromthe kerb following estimates of production surpluses next year. It was indicated at $746/$748, albeit in very thin business.
